summary: MP-heal number popup of the battle UI: a UI object that owns three per-digit animation-reference groups and six 0xA8-byte number widgets, one per queued MP-heal number. The batch name is stale - the readable tree now calls this class Battle_MpHealPopup (its dtor 0x0046B1B0 installs vtable 0x00772BEC and its layout string is 'pop_mpheal_%d').
evidence: Battle_MpHealPopup_Dtor (0x0046B1B0) stores vtable 0x00772BEC at +0, runs std_destroy_range(self+0x13C, 0x003D2580, 0xA8, 6) and std_destroy_range(self+0x4C, 0x003E04BC, 0x50, 3), then Ui_Object_DtorBase (0x001A6768). Battle_Popup_InitMpHealPopup (0x0046ADF8) constructs the six 0xA8-byte widgets in a loop (asm 0x0046AE44..0x0046AEB8, stride 0xA8, count 6) and formats 'pop_mpheal_%d'. The batch size 320 (highest strong field + 4) is only a lower bound: the dtor proves the object reaches 0x13C + 6*0xA8 = 0x52C = 1324 bytes.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Battle_MpHealPopup_Dtor stores the literal 0x00772BEC (DAT_0046b1f8) at +0; the vtable holds Battle_Popup_InitMpHealPopup (0x0046ADF8) and Battle_Popup_PrepareMpHealNumberPanes (0x0046AF30).

fields.name: digitPaneRefs
fields.evidence: Three 0x50-byte elements at +0x4C destroyed with Ui_LayoutRef_Release (0x003E04BC) and constructed with Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor (0x003E0454); Battle_Popup_PrepareMpHealNumberPanes hides them with func_003E043C(self + 0x4C + 0x50*i, 0) for i = 0..2, i.e. one animation-reference group per MP digit.

fields.name: numberWidgets
fields.evidence: Six embedded 0xA8-byte UI widgets at +0x13C (dtor: std_destroy_range(self+0x13C, 0x003D2580, 0xA8, 6); ctor loop at asm 0x0046AE44 with stride 0xA8, count 6). Each is initialised by 0x001A6520 (layout pointer at +0x30, pane at +0x4C, cached pane at +0x50, Ui_AnimRef at +0x54) and destroyed by the thunk 0x003D2580 into maybe_Ui_IconButton_Dtor (vtable 0x007699DC). Kept as an opaque byte array because no recovered class has the 0xA8-byte layout.

summary: Battle action model: the per-action 3D model/attachment object created by the two factory functions, holding the model vtable, the node/attachment tables and a two-byte visibility mode. The batch name is stale - the readable tree now calls this class Battle_ActionModel (vtable 0x00774BF4).
evidence: Battle_ActionModel_CreateDefault (0x00485874) and Battle_ActionModel_CreateWithFlag (0x00485390) both call Battle_ActionModel_CreateBase (0x001CC3EC), store vtable 0x00774BF4 at +0 and write the flag bytes +0xF22/+0xF23; Battle_ActionModel_SetVisibilityMode (0x00485824) is the only writer of +0xF22. Size 0xF24 = 3876 matches the highest field +0xF23. structs.json already carries the same class as Battle_ActionModel with 26 fields, so only the three batch offsets are named here.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Both factories store the literal 0x00774BF4 (DAT_004853ac / DAT_00485894) at +0; the vtable slots are the Battle_ActionModel_* methods (0x00485108 NotifyEffect, 0x004853EC UpdateAttachmentVisibility, 0x00485824 SetVisibilityMode).

fields.name: visibilityMode
fields.evidence: Battle_ActionModel_SetVisibilityMode stores its argument here; Battle_ActionModel_UpdateAttachmentVisibility compares it with 2 to pick the special path, and both factories clear it to 0.

fields.name: maybe_visibilityFlag
fields.evidence: Write-only in the recovered code: SetVisibilityMode sets it to 0 when switching to mode 1 from state 0x1A5 (and then refreshes the node list through vtable +0x11C), otherwise to 1; both factories clear it. No read proves whether it means visible, dirty or suppressed.

summary: Battle command/message window flow driver: holds the current step id, the condition sub-state and a pointer to the active flow-step record, and opens/hides the selection, item-name, row-info and confirm windows for that step.
evidence: Battle_UiFlow_UpdateState (0x002DC8D0) is a dense switch on self->f_1A8 over 0x39, 0x3A..0x45, 0x47, 0x6F, 0xDC, each case calling one of the 24 Battle_UiFlow_* step handlers; Battle_UiFlow_EvaluateCondition (0x002DFA1C) switches on self->f_1A4 over 0x1A..0x27; Battle_UiFlow_AdvanceStep (0x002DF590) walks the step list reached through self->f_1B4 and matches step+0x1B8 against self->f_1A8. Size 440 = highest field +0x1B4 + 4.

fields.name: conditionState
fields.evidence: Battle_UiFlow_EvaluateCondition switches on it with cases 0x1A..0x27 and answers 'row selected', 'item exists', 'window idle' style questions for each; never written in the recovered code, so it is set by the (unrecovered) flow ctor.

fields.name: stepId
fields.evidence: Battle_UiFlow_UpdateState switches on it (0x39, 0x3A..0x45, 0x47, 0x6F, 0xDC) and dispatches to the matching step handler; Battle_UiFlow_AdvanceStep compares it with the step record's +0x1B8 to select the current step.

fields.name: currentStep
fields.evidence: Pointer to the active flow-step record: its +0x7C is the row index passed to func_002AB62C(battleWork+0x4254, index), +0x10 is a 0x59-byte 'entry used' array, +0x78 an SE handle, +0x80 a count, +0x84/+0x85 flags. AdvanceStep also uses its +0x00/+0x04 list head and stores the matched step at +0x0C.

summary: Battle member-widget interface (secondary vtable 0x0075CDD4 of the 60776-byte Battle_Ui): the sound and row-style slots a battle party member widget implements. The batch name is stale - the readable tree now calls these slots Battle_Ui_Member_* / Battle_Ui_MemberAnim_PlaySe*.
evidence: The four recovered functions are vtable slots of 0x0075CDD4, which struct_db attributes to Battle_Ui (60776 bytes): slot 0 = 0x003CB6FC, slot 1 = 0x003CB4EC, slot 2 = 0x003CCD90, slot 4 = 0x003CB148. Two of the three batch offsets are struct_db artefacts of vtable-slot arithmetic ((*self+0x48)*4 and (*self+0x150)*4). The real object is the Battle_Ui member widget and is at least 0x137B bytes (+0x12D8 actor pointer, +0x137A member byte), so the batch size 4736 is only a lower bound.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot48
fields.evidence: Not a field: struct_db multiplied the vtable slot offset in (**(code**)(*self + 0x48))(self,0) by 4. 0x48 is a vtable slot of the member widget (it returns the row object), not a byte offset into the object.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot150
fields.evidence: Not a field: struct_db multiplied the vtable slot offset in (**(code**)(*self + 0x150))(self) by 4. 0x150 is a vtable slot (it returns the record passed to 0x00488638), not a byte offset.

fields.name: maybe_actionResult
fields.evidence: Real: asm 0x003CB150/0x003CB154 computes self+0x127C and passes it as arg2 to 0x00488638, which writes a u16 result at +4 and a flag at +0x53 of it. The record is therefore larger than 4 bytes; only its start is known, so the extent is left at the batch width.

summary: State block of a 2D battle unit: cancels the unit's current sub-action through its own vtable and tracks the active action slot, reset to -1 when idle.
evidence: Battle2DUnit_StateBlock_Reset (0x005A1ED8) is vtable 0x0077ED84 slot 5 (slot 6 is 0x005A1D48 maybe_Battle2DUnit_ShowActionPopup); it calls (**(code**)(*self + 0x34))(self,0) and then self[0x497] = -1. Size 4704 = 0x1260 = highest field +0x125C + 4.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot34
fields.evidence: Not a field: struct_db multiplied the vtable slot offset in (**(code**)(*self + 0x34))(self,0) by 4. 0x34 is a vtable slot (cancel/stop the current sub-action), not a byte offset.

fields.name: maybe_currentActionSlot
fields.evidence: Battle2DUnit_StateBlock_Reset writes -1 here after cancelling the sub-action; -1 is the 'none' sentinel the project uses for slot indices (e.g. PartyMember +0x11C equipped slots). No other read proves the meaning.

summary: One element of a battle action animation sequence (the 'confuse' / attack-start / back-jump / use-item element family): holds the actor it animates and a finished flag, and is driven through a 10-slot script vtable. The batch name is stale - structs.json already carries the same layout as Battle_Action (1384 bytes, base Ui_ObjectBase).
evidence: Vtable 0x0076C414 (installed by Battle_ActionAnim_ConfuseElementCtor 0x003FB868 as 0x0076C410) has 10 slots: 0 dtor, 1 Play, 3 PlayAnimIfAvailable, 4..6 script slots 0x00193C6C/0x00193CD8/0x00193CD4, 7..9 0x0062A704/0x0062A714/0x0062A70C. The same two offsets +0x28/+0x2C appear in structs.json's Battle_Action (1384 bytes, base Ui_ObjectBase, +0x28 read 69 times), so this batch class is a 48-byte fragment of that object.

fields.name: actor
fields.evidence: Battle_ActionAnim_ConfuseElement_Play calls (**(code**)(*self->f_28 + 0x84))(self->f_28, "confuse") to play a named animation; Battle_ActionAnim_CommitWeaponNodes reads self->f_28->f_273 (a unit index for func_002AB698(battleWork+0x4254, index)) and self->f_28->f_224 (a Model_Equip*). No recovered class has that layout, so the type stays void*.

fields.name: isFinished
fields.evidence: Battle_ActionAnim_ConfuseElement_Play sets it to 1 when the animation dispatcher returns 0 (nothing was played); Battle_Action reads it as a 'done' flag and clears it to 0 when the element restarts.

summary: Battle scene unit-model slot table: three 0xC-byte slots, each holding the unit model created for one model variant and the variant byte handed to the model's vtable slot 0x68.
evidence: maybe_Battle_SceneInit_Shared (0x004BAC3C) allocates a 0x144-byte unit model (Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x144,...)), installs one of the three unit-model vtables 0x007759FC / 0x00775AB8 / 0x00775xxx depending on arg6->f_768 (399, 0x1A5, 0x350), then does owner += variant*0xC, (**(code**)(*result + 0x68))(result, owner->f_a4) and owner->f_a0 = result. The 0xC stride means the object has three such slots (+0xA0, +0xAC, +0xB8), so the batch size 168 is only a lower bound.

fields.name: unitModel
fields.evidence: maybe_Battle_SceneInit_Shared stores the freshly created 0x144-byte unit model here (owner->f_a0 = result) after configuring it; the same function reads the slot back through the model vtable.

fields.name: modelVariant
fields.evidence: Passed to the unit model's vtable slot 0x68 ((**(code**)(*result + 0x68))(result, owner->f_a4)) right before the model pointer is stored; the variant is chosen from arg6->f_768 (399 / 0x1A5 / 0x350).

summary: Battle damage popup element: a script-driven 10-slot action element that plays the damage animation and sound and keeps a link to the actor it is attached to.
evidence: Vtable 0x00764240: slot 0 = Battle_DamagePopup_DeletingDestructor (0x0032CCB4), slot 1 = maybe_Battle_Damage_PlayAnimAndSe (0x0032CBF8), slot 3 = maybe_Battle_DamagePopup_DetachActor (0x0032CC54), slots 4..9 = the same script slots (0x00193C6C/0x00193CD8/0x00193CD4/0x0062A704/0x0062A714/0x0062A70C) as the Battle_ActionAnim element family. Size 44 = highest field +0x28 + 4.

fields.name: actor
fields.evidence: maybe_Battle_DamagePopup_DetachActor tests func_00669DD4(self->f_28) (asm 0x00669DD4 reads +0x160, +0x568, +0x56C of it and returns a comparison) and then calls func_005E7848(self->f_28, 0, 1) (asm 0x005E7848 forwards to the object's +0x60). Both are actor/scene-node accessors, so this is the popup's actor link.

summary: Battle item-target window: a 440-byte command window that remembers which battle unit the item page is aimed at and greys out targets whose state blocks items.
evidence: Only one function is recovered: Battle_Item_CanTargetActor (0x003906D8), which resolves func_002AB62C(battleWork+0x4254, self->f_1b4) and rejects the unit when Battle_Unit_HasState (0x00639954, still named Ui_TextLayout_IsTypeAccepted) reports 0x10F, 0x9C or 0x9A. Size 440 = highest field +0x1B4 + 4. The class is not Battle_UiFlow even though both are 440 bytes: here +0x1B4 is loaded as a plain index (asm 0x003906F8 ldr r1,[r4,#0x1b4]), while Battle_UiFlow dereferences its +0x1B4 as a pointer.

fields.name: targetActorIndex
fields.evidence: Loaded with ldr r1,[r4,#0x1b4] and passed as the index to func_002AB62C(battleWork+0x4254, index), which returns the battle unit; the result is then tested with the item-blocking state ids 0x10F/0x9C/0x9A.
